profile.reading: This OpenStreetMap record in Maricopa County, Arizona, near Mesa, is labeled Myndshift Technologies and tagged as a data center, but the same record also carries a healthcare specialty tag for neurology, an unusual pairing that points toward a healthcare or health technology office rather than a facility built to house server racks and cooling infrastructure for outside customers. A domain search finds two different signals for the Myndshift name: myndshift.com is currently listed for sale on a domain marketplace, suggesting that address is not in active use by an operating company, while myndshift.io is a live, registered domain that actively blocks automated access, which is at least consistent with an active but non public web presence. Neither result was sufficient to confirm what kind of organization currently occupies this Maricopa County address, what it does, or whether it operates any data center infrastructure at all. Given the healthcare tag on the same record, the more plausible reading is a small office for a health technology or clinical services business running its own internal systems, not a commercial or enterprise data center. This entry records that uncertainty honestly rather than describing capacity, tenants or infrastructure that could not be verified.

reading.body:
A single OpenStreetMap record in Maricopa County, Arizona labels one address as both a data center and a neurology office, and no operator, capacity, or web presence could be confirmed.

The conflict is the finding. A commercial data center and a clinical neurology practice are not the same kind of tenant, and the same record carrying both tags means at least one is wrong. The domain evidence leans the same way: myndshift.com is parked for sale, and myndshift.io blocks automated access, so neither confirms an operating company at this address. Reverse geocoding returned only a road name with no business match.

For AI infrastructure this matters as a negative result. A data center that cannot be tied to an operator, a power figure, or a floor area cannot be counted toward compute. Arizona has 56 mapped data center locations and only 4 with published megawatt figures totaling 512 MW, so the state's confirmed capacity already rests on a small disclosed subset. Adding an unverified entry would inflate that subset without adding a single megawatt.

What the data does not cover is anything about the actual occupant. It does not establish that no data center exists here, only that none was confirmed. It does not give power, cooling, floor space, or tenants, and it does not say what Myndshift Technologies does. The honest reading is a probable small healthcare or health technology office running internal systems, and it should stay out of any model of Arizona AI compute until an operator publishes specifications.
